title: What's a Tensor? — Dan Fleisch (12 min)
note: The clearest geometric intuition for where the word 'tensor' comes from — built from arrows, shadows, and basis vectors with household objects. It teaches the physics tensor (coordinate-system machinery we don't need to operate chips), so treat it as optional origin-of-the-word; for operations, a tensor is just a multidimensional array.

title: What Is a Tensor? — see it in numpy
note: Reads rank and shape straight off numpy arrays, computes the footprint formula, and charts the rank → memory blow-up (rank 3 punches through a chip's HBM). Pure numpy, runs on CPU.

title: Reason about rank and the memory bill
prompt: An activation tensor has shape [batch=8, seq=8192, hidden=4096] in bf16. State its rank, compute its footprint in bytes, then explain why doubling the sequence length and why adding one more dimension each affect HBM differently. Tie it back to why a longer-context job can OOM when a shorter one fit on the same chip.
